newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Bullion knocks SAfrica golds, industrials end weak too.
newsitem.headline: Bullion knocks SAfrica golds, industrials end weak too.

text.p: South African gold shares finished more than three percent weaker in Friday's quiet trade after bullion slid to 12-year lows, dealers said.

The local gold index which broke through the 1,000 level on June 27, and shed more than three percent at start of trade on Friday in the wake of bullion's overnight slide, finished down 33.1 points or 3.6 percent, at 952.1.
The dealers said the gold market had started sagging late on Thursday on new of Australian central bank gold sales and had remained vulnerable to further losses.
Spot gold late Thursday was down to its lowest levels since early December 1985 when gold was recovering from the low of $281 an ounce seen in February 1985.
The dealers said bullion's woes had quickly permeated through the market's gold shares, forcing a majority of them to sink to new year lows.
Bullion fixed at $324.45 an ounce in London on Friday, making the fix the lowest since late December 1985.
But not only golds took a bashing on Friday in the South African market.
Dealers said industrials followed suit, sagging in sympathy with the precious metal amid some profit-taking following their recent bounce.
Dealers said weakness in the industrial shares was also as a result of some consolidation in a market needing to cool off.
The industrial index ended down 27.9 points at 8,801.9, while the all-share dipped 35.2 points to finish at 7,368.0.
In the broader market declines led advances by about 223 to 131, while 21 shares hit new highs and 34 slid to new lows.
Dealers said overall market volumes were moderate with 600 million rand worth of shares exchanging hands at the close.
